summary: The Ohio Information Technology Centers (OITC) argue that Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) should remain eligible for E‑Rate funding, citing cost‑effectiveness, operational benefits, and the need for oversight rather than cuts. The Schools, Health & Libraries Broadband Coalition argues that Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) are essential, cost‑effective, and should remain an eligible Category Two service in the E‑Rate program. Ohio OITC comments argue that Managed Internal Broadband Service (MIBS) is essential for all school districts, regardless of size or location, to meet cybersecurity requirements and maintain reliable connectivity. The Ohio Information Technology Centers (OITC) argue that Managed Internal Broadband Services (MIBS) should remain an eligible E‑Rate Category II service, that a clearer definition of eligible MIBS services is needed, and that targeted oversight and data‑driven review will address waste, fraud, and abuse without cutting funding.
